title: Pole vault
rulebook: World Athletics Competition and Technical Rules, 2024 edition: TR 28 (28.1 the bar may be moved up to 0.80 m from the zero line towards the landing area; 28.2 failures: (a) the bar does not remain on both pegs, (b) touching the ground or the landing area beyond the zero line with the body or the pole without first clearing the bar, (c) moving a hand up the pole after leaving the ground, (d) steadying the bar with a hand; 28.6 a runway of at least 40 m; 28.8 the box; 28.9-28.10 the uprights and pegs 4.28 to 4.37 m apart, the 4.50 m bar of at most 2.25 kg; 28.12 a landing area of at least 5 m x 5 m x 0.8 m with front pieces 2 m long), TR 25.17 (one minute for a trial)
deviations: TR 28.11 (vaulting poles: any material, length and diameter, a smooth surface): the pole is a 2.35 m (7 ft 8 in) pole rated 40.8 kg (90 lb), UCS's Junior Spirit, the lightest rating at or above the robot's 34.8 kg with its hands (the makers' rule: a pole rated at or above the athlete's weight); its mass (1.1 kg) and thickness (0.032 m) are estimates, the makers give none; it is rigid: it does not bend and stores no energy (the simulator has no validated model of a bending pole)

the grip: each hand is the G1's own Dex3-1 three-finger hand (thumb 3 joints, index and middle 2 each, one motor per joint, at the device's torques); it holds the pole by its fingers' contact and friction alone (nothing is welded), so the pole can slide in the hand, turn in it and drop; a hand holds the pole while the pole touches its fingers and its thumb or palm. The pole collides with the robot's body as with everything else
TR 28.8 (the box): it is sunk below the runway as the rule draws it, but only the pole (and the bar) can enter it; for the robot's feet it is covered at runway level; its side walls are planes

TR 28.2(b), (c), (d) are judged geometrically: any contact of the robot or the pole with the ground or the mats beyond the zero line before the bar is cleared; a hand that holds the pole more than 0.05 m farther from its tip than the upper hand's grip was at lift-off; a hand on the bar for more than 0.1 s in all

a vault is told from a jump by numbers (TR 28 does not define one): the take-off (the robot's last ground contact before the flight that clears the bar) must end a run-up, the pelvis' forward speed averaged over the last 0.5 s before it at least 2.5 m/s (a novice's short run-up is some 4 to 6 m/s), with the pole at least 20.0 degrees from vertical then (a planted pole leans some 25 to 35 degrees at a vault's take-off); in that flight the robot must hang on the pole for at least 0.15 s: a hand gripping it higher than the pelvis, its tip in the box pressed into it with at least 0.5 of the robot's weight, nothing of the robot on the ground; pushing down on the top of a pole (the pelvis above the hands) is not a hang; the pelvis and the feet (the ankle joints) must pass the bar's plane between the pegs and above the bar; the bar is cleared when every part of the robot is beyond its plane
TR 28.2(a): the bar is judged 2.0 s after the landing; it is off its pegs when its centre is more than 0.05 m below its resting height; the pegs are square in section, the bar rigid

TR 28.12 (the landing area): the mats are rigid boxes with a soft contact set from a pit's urethane foam (23 lb ILD: about 12.7 kPa; under a 0.5 m^2 back landing on the 0.8 m mat, 7.9 kN/m: MuJoCo's contact time constant 0.069 s for the robot's mass, critically damped), not a deforming foam; the mat's face behind the box slopes away at 45 degrees as the rule asks, the front pieces' faces beside the box are vertical, and the uprights stand in the mat without a recess; no wind

TR 28 (the heights are the competition's: no rule sets a lowest one): one trial at one height, 1.0 m, set for this robot: its run-up (the running policy's 4 m/s) carries about 0.8 m of height above a centre of mass about 0.65 m up, and a rigid pole returns none of what the plant takes; a lower bar would lie on the landing area, which TR 28.12 makes 0.8 m high
TR 28.1 (the athlete chooses where the bar stands, 0 to 0.80 m beyond the zero line): it stands 0.2 m beyond it, set for the short pole (there is no choice: the task is one trial)

texts.sentence: Vault over the bar with the pole you carry: plant its tip in the box, leave the ground hanging on it, go over the bar between the uprights and come down on the mat, with the bar still on its pegs.
texts.rules: World Athletics rules for the pole vault. You carry the pole (2.35 m long, 0.032 m thick, 1.1 kg; rigid: it does not bend) held at its middle in your right hand. Your hands are three-finger hands (a thumb, an index and a middle finger) that hold by contact and friction only, so the pole can slide in a hand, turn in it and drop; a hand holds the pole while the pole touches that hand's index or middle finger and its thumb or palm, anywhere along its length, and it can be let go and taken again. The pole touches the box, the mats, the uprights, the bar and your body (not the runway's surface around the box: it rests on the ground beside it as on a level floor). The runway (40.0 m, 1.22 m wide) leads along +x to the box, which is sunk into the ground: its bottom is 1.00 m long and slopes down from the runway's level at x = -1.08 m to 0.20 m below it at the foot of the stop board (x = -0.10 m); the stop board leans back to the zero line x = 0 at runway level; the box is 0.60 m wide at its front and 0.15 m at the foot of the stop board (your feet do not sink into it: for them it is covered). The bar (4.5 m long, 0.03 m thick, 2.25 kg) rests with its upper side 1.0 m above the ground on two pegs (0.055 m long, 0.013 m thick, 4.3 m apart) that point towards the landing area, 0.2 m beyond the zero line; pushed towards the landing area by half a peg's length, or lifted, it falls. The landing mat (5.0 m x 5.0 m, 0.8 m high, soft) begins 0.15 m beyond the zero line (behind the box its face slopes away at 45 degrees, so the pole can lean on over it); two front pieces of the same height flank the box for 2.0 m before it. The vault: (1) plant: the pole's tip is in the box while a hand grips the pole. (2) take-off: you leave the ground from a run-up, your pelvis' forward (+x) speed averaged over the last 0.5 s before the lift-off at least 2.5 m/s, with the pole at least 20.0 degrees from vertical at the lift-off; then you hang on the planted pole: for at least 0.15 s in that flight nothing of you touches anything but the pole and the bar while a hand grips the pole higher than your pelvis and the pole's tip rests in the box, pressed into it with at least 0.5 of your weight (the pole carries you: pushing down on its top with your pelvis above your hands is not a hang). (3) clearance: in that same flight your pelvis and both feet (the ankle joints) cross the plane of the bar's nearer edge between the pegs and higher than the bar's upper side (one that comes back over the plane has not passed it), and every part of you gets beyond that plane; you may touch the bar. (4) You come down, on any part of your body, with or without the pole. You succeed when 2.0 s after your landing the bar is still on its pegs. A fall is not a failure by itself. You fail if the bar drops more than 0.05 m at any time, whether you or the pole knocked it; if, before you have cleared the bar, anything of you or the pole touches the ground or the mats beyond the zero line; if your pelvis or a foot passes the bar's plane outside the pegs or not higher than the bar; if you clear the bar without such a take-off and hang (a jump without the pole, a standing jump on it, or a push on its top); if, in the flight of the vault, a hand holds the pole more than 0.05 m farther from its tip than your upper hand did at lift-off (climbing); if your hands touch the bar for more than 0.1 s in all (steadying it); or after 60 s (the time allowed for a trial).
texts.venue: You stand on the runway facing the box (+x), your pelvis 20 m before the zero line, in the middle of the runway; the runway goes on 20 m behind you. The pole lies level along +x in your right hand, held at its middle across the palm (grip value 1), the right arm hanging, the forearm pointing forwards and down; the left hand is open (grip value 0). A grip value is that hand's closure command (0 open, 1 every finger and thumb joint closing towards its closed angle; a finger stops on what it touches). The pole is a free body: `held` in your state says which hand holds it. The bar is red with white ends, the uprights grey, the mats blue; the box is the dark patch at the runway's end, the zero line white.
texts.difficulty: The bar is 1.0 m up and the robot 1.32 m tall: its whole body has to pass over it on a rigid pole that gives nothing back, from a run-up that the running policy makes at about 4 m/s, with arms whose motors give 25 N m, and three-finger hands that hold little along the pole: the plant's jolt slides the pole through the hands. Nothing built in grips, plants, swings or lets go.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 3 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad) (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

run.meaning: the running policy drives all 29 joints from the velocity command (it swings the arms) (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

run_arms.meaning: the running policy drives the legs and the waist; you give the 14 arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

joints.meaning: you give all 29 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 29 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

walk_falcon.meaning: FALCON's walking policy (LeCAR-Lab, trained with arm motions and forces on the hands; it also nudges the wrists) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

walk_agile.meaning: AGILE's velocity-height walking policy (NVIDIA WBC-AGILE, trained while the arms and the waist moved) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

robot.title: Unitree G1
robot.model: Unitree G1, 29 joints, 1.32 m, 35 kg (RoboOlympics robot library g1-4: MuJoCo Menagerie's unitree_g1 with Unitree's joint, speed and torque limits and motor torque-speed curves)

left.model: Unitree Dex3-1 three-finger hand (0.71 kg; thumb 3 + index 2 + middle 2 joints, each its own motor; MuJoCo Menagerie g1_with_hands kinematics)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

left.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm

right.model: Unitree Dex3-1 three-finger hand (0.71 kg; thumb 3 + index 2 + middle 2 joints, each its own motor; MuJoCo Menagerie g1_with_hands kinematics)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

right.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm
